text_summary.body: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel; Zerubbabel and Jeshua began to build the house of God, and the prophets were with them, helping them.

setting.body: Haggai dates his first oracle to 1/VI of Darius's second year and the start of work to 24/VI (Hag 1:1, 15); on Parker and Dubberstein's table these are 29 August and 21 September 520. Zechariah's first oracle is in the eighth month (Zech 1:1). Darius had spent 522–521 suppressing revolts (Behistun).

constraints.textual_assertion: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month
assumptions: Babylonian Nisan-based regnal years (as for Ezra 6:15): year 2 = 3 April 520 – 22 March 519 (Parker & Dubberstein table). Month VI began 29 August 520, so 1/VI = 29 Aug and 24/VI (Hag 1:15) = 21 Sep 520.

competing_reconstructions.label: Resumption of a work begun in 536
competing_reconstructions.summary: "Began to build" (5:2) means the building proper after an earlier foundation.

competing_reconstructions.label: The real beginning of the rebuilding
competing_reconstructions.summary: The foundation was laid on 24/IX of Darius's second year (Hag 2:18).

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik summarises Haggai's rebuke (Hag 1:2–10) and contrasts Zechariah's concern with the people's spiritual state; Adeney notes that Darius was occupied securing his throne.
